content.comment_body: [user_name], I am working with heating analog modules in [product_name]. [url] A trend is displayed. I have tried many approaches to enable a trend view. Could anyone advise how to set up a trend view?
I did not create the graphic; LSC generates it when a PI controller is used in a [product_name] program running in simulation mode.
Are there options to display trends on a TD or another HMI? Or is this only available from version [version_no] onward?
I am not aware of any available solutions. Using LWE, it might be possible if you are familiar with HTML5, though I am not. Apparently, from [product_name] [version_no], this should be possible...

A trend view can be easily accessed for AIx or AQx modules for BM or TDE. Go to the menu showing time, inputs, and outputs. On the analog input or output, select a desired signal (e.g., AI1) and press Enter to view the trend. For showing a block output, connect it to an unused analog output in the program. If this trend view does not suit your needs, look for PC Modbus clients with integrated trend view and configure [product_name] as a Modbus server. For trend display on an HMI, search for HMIs that support trend view and the necessary communication protocol. Regards, [user_name]

Here is a link to a video showing a simulation of how the Trend View might appear on an HMI Basic Panel. The video file is too large to be posted directly. Trend view simulation for HMI Basic Panel [url]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing difficulties with visualizing analog signal trends using [product_name] and seeks advice for trend view setups—either natively, through simulation, or on external HMI devices. The discussion reflects uncertainty about which product versions support built-in trend visualization and suggests considering external solutions if built-in features are limited.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a simple and accessible trend visualization for analog channels, whether via the [product_name] system itself, its simulation environment, or compatible HMI devices.
